chapter_theme: The nature of those who have reached (அணைந்தோர் தன்மை): told mostly in the first person, they are free of stain, pride, caste and bonds; the Lord has entered and ruled them, birth and karma are cut, Yama can be fought off, worldly sweetness turns sour beside his bliss, and the mind's spreading and drawing in, stilled with speech, is release.
structure_note: Verses in the first person of one who has reached alternate with descriptions of such people (2957, 2969, 2970). Several verses chain by repeated words (பணிந்துநின்றேன், பிணக்கறுத்தான்). The last verse (2981) sums the mind's movement as tapas, breath and life, and its end as mukti.

2957.reading: For those who by knowledge set Nandi firmly in love, holding steady, there is no impurity, no stain, no pride or self-regard, no caste, no qualities to take on, no good to seek.
2957.nuance: குலமில்லை denies caste or lineage to the one who has reached. நலமில்லை is surprising after a list of faults; it may mean no worldly good is needed, or that such a one is past good and bad alike. பலமன்னி is obscure, perhaps 'abiding in strength' or 'with the fruit secured'.

2958.reading: I have left birth and the bond called kinship; I am free; God and I have become one; I want no more gain that comes and perishes; I have seen Siva, the rich refuge.
2958.nuance: உறவு என்னும் பாசம் makes kinship itself a bond. கடவுளும் நானும் ஒன்றானேன் is a plain statement of union, though how 'one' is meant (identity or inseparability) is the long dispute between Vedanta and Siddhanta, which the verse doesn't enter.

2959.reading: Our land has cane in the mill, nectar, sugar and the cool water of groves; the lovely woman who makes a form like the eye of a peacock's feather lacks for nothing.
2959.nuance: The verse reads at first as praise of a fertile land and a fortunate woman. In this chapter it is likely symbolic: the land as the body or the state reached, its sweets and waters as bliss and nectar, the woman as Shakti or the soul. பீலிக்கண் (the eye of a peacock feather) is sometimes taken as a light seen in meditation. None of this can be fixed from the verse.

2960.reading: From now no one can harm me; the glorious Lord came and entered my mind; I have come to know the knowledge in which, apart from wandering there in joy, I go near no one now.
2960.nuance: Lines 3 and 4 are hard: சீராடி may be playing like a cherished child, and யார்படும் சாரா may be 'not approaching anyone' or 'what no one reaches'.

2961.reading: I have parted from the bond that Brahma tied; I have learned the state that goes on the way of Siva; I have cut down karma with the sharp sword of the mind; I have broken the city and press on ahead.
2961.nuance: Brahma's bond is birth into a body. புரம் (the city) may be the body, or may echo Siva's burning of the three cities, taken as the three malas. அயில் மன வாள் (the sharp sword of mind) parallels the sword of knowledge in 2968.

2962.reading: See, there is one God for the world; see, the one is what is life to the world; see that it is good: now, having eaten the fruit நமசிவாய, how sweet it has been to me!
2962.nuance: Each line opens with a call to 'see' (கண்டீர்) and the last turns to the speaker's own tasting (கண்டேற்கு). The five-letter mantra as a fruit makes knowing it a matter of taste, as in 2946.

2963.reading: The one with matted hair who wears the moon with the snake came and ruled me and became a jewel-lamp, the rare thing with neither end nor beginning; he settled in my mind and cut away my confusion.

2964.reading: No one knows the purpose of the Lord who was within us of old, who stays there seeing tall Mal and Brahma; if he breaks forth and appears there and the mind becomes empty, what stood there as a fragment becomes a mere thicket.
2964.nuance: The verse is obscure. One reading takes Vishnu and Brahma as lesser lords the inner Lord oversees, and the last line as saying that, to a mind emptied, the separate gods are as worthless as scrub. விண்டு may be 'splitting open' or a form of Vishnu's name.

2965.reading: Apart from the love that Mother and Father bore, who knows Mother and Father, and who knows me? With Mother and Father and me together, I came to serve the Mother and the Father.
2965.nuance: Mother and Father are traditionally Shakti and Siva. என்னை may be 'me' or 'what'. புரிந்தேன் can be served, desired or understood, so the last line may also say the speaker came to understand them.

2966.reading: The whorl it took, the summit of the great mountain, the gods, the lord of the gods, the First and those of the eight directions came and are in the palm of my hand; now I am saved and done.
2966.nuance: கொண்ட சுழி may be the coil of kundalini or the crown's whorl, and குலவரை உச்சி the summit of Meru, often taken as the top of the head in yogic reading. The whole cosmos held in the hand is a claim to mastery, or to the cosmos being found within. உண்டனர் is read as 'they are there'; it could also be 'they ate'.

2967.reading: He himself stands as the directions and the gods; he himself stands as the northern mountain and the origin; he himself stands as body, life and tattvas; he himself is also the Lord in the world.
2967.nuance: தானே may be the Lord, as in many such lists, or, in this chapter, the one who has reached and become all, following 2966. The verse doesn't say which.

2968.reading: If Yama comes I will strike him with the sword of knowledge; if Siva comes, it is sure I will go with him; I cut long ago the strong karma that brings birth; who can stand against a mind into which tapas has come?
2968.nuance: The two comings set death and Siva side by side: one is driven off, the other followed. பவம் is birth or worldly becoming.

2969.reading: Those whose minds have become Siva and who have destroyed the three malas become pure Siva and do not touch the bondage of malam; they see no turning, no wavering, no strife, holding that sound and the supreme bindu are themselves.
2969.nuance: The three malas are traditionally anava, karma and maya. சுத்தும் சிலகும் is obscure and may be corrupt. The last line may say that nada and parabindu are themselves, or that they are He; either way it places these states within, not as things to reach.

2970.reading: In the heart of those without thinking and forgetting dwells the Pure One who cuts away karma's clinging; if one goes seeking that Pure One and gets to think of him, he becomes far off.
2970.nuance: The paradox: he dwells where neither thinking nor forgetting is, so to think of him is to set him at a distance. நீளியன் may instead mean 'vast' or 'great', which would make the last line praise rather than warning.

2971.reading: When I called and praised him as Siva Peruman, he came and stood as the Lord of tapas; the Lord of undoing, the master who owns me: I stood bowing to the Lord of becoming.
2971.nuance: The verse plays on names: சிவ, தவ, அவ and பவ before பெருமான். பவன் (Bhava) is a name of Siva; அவ may be 'the destroyer', from அவம் (undoing), though its sense is unsure.

2972.reading: I stood bowing to the Lord, first and supreme; I stood resolved, wanting nothing else from now; I stood having put on the primal Lord as my body; I stood calmed, having seen the nature of Siva.
2972.nuance: Each line opens a stance with நின்றேன். அணிந்து நின்றேன் உடல் ஆதிப்பிரானை may be wearing the Lord as one's body (taking his form), or adorning the body with him, as with ash and emblems.

2973.reading: When my heart joined the Lord's two feet and I praised him beforehand, birth was cut away entirely; the Lord, who has no mind of his own, broke up the fate written for me and ended my discord.
2973.nuance: தலைவிதி is fate, the writing on the head. தன் நெஞ்சம் இல்லாத் தலைவன் is obscure: the Lord beyond mind, or one without self-interest. பிணக்கு can be discord, entanglement or the strife of rival creeds.

2974.reading: Nandi ended my discord, cut away disease, old age and the reckoning that is counted, and ruled me; when he ended my discord and the sorrow that had come along with me from before, I fell to bowing: it was Siva who had come.
2974.nuance: The verse picks up பிணக்கறுத்தான் from 2973. எண்ணும் கணக்கு may be the counting of one's days or the account of karma; முன்வந்த துன்பம் (sorrow come with me from before) is likely the karma of past births.

2975.reading: Siva came with the throng of gods, cut off the bond that stood so that birth would come, and he, my Father, the First Lord who ruled and graced me, came and was caught within me.
2975.nuance: அகப்பட்டவாறு (how he got caught) turns the usual picture round: the soul seized by the Lord here holds the Lord.

2976.reading: In a body where cane and honey are mixed, the bliss that is bud and fragrance: once the heart, longing, saw it laid open, the cane turned bitter and the honey sour.
2976.nuance: Cane and honey are first the body's sweet pleasures, then spoiled by the greater bliss. வெளியுற may be 'openly' or 'in the inner space'. The verse sets Siva's bliss against worldly pleasure, as the concept's gloss has it, rather than condemning the body.

2977.reading: Having followed chariyai and the rest and then turned back, singing the riches the Generous One set in me in his love, since I see all that is done as Siva, I have passed beyond the womb with nothing in my hands.
2977.nuance: Chariyai and the rest are the four Saiva paths. மீட்டு may mean turning back from them or being brought back. கைவளம் இன்றி may be 'without any wealth in hand' (without merit of my own) or 'without the skill of my hands'.

2978.reading: When, turned back, the fire went deep into the lotus and was set in the bowl as a lamp that needs no trimming, one woman, crown-jewel of the worlds, took it on, and it came into the hand of a man who had died.
2978.nuance: Very obscure. The lamp that needs no trimming (தூண்டா விளக்கு) is a common image of the self-lit inner light; the lotus is a centre of the yogic body; the woman is likely Shakti; the man who died may be the one who has died to self. Any fuller reading would be invented.

2979.reading: There is a river, a waterfall and a tank within; Siva's way is fine, and so is its colour; the excellent thing is a share with the lady slender as a creeper, with rounded breasts, and also stays apart.
2979.nuance: ஆறு may be river or six, the six centres of the yogic body; the waterfall and inner tank are likely the nectar's flow. நூறே may be 'fine as powder' or 'a hundred'. The last lines give Siva as half of the Goddess and yet distinct, the Siddhanta position.

2980.reading: Melting in love I weep and cry out; with my very bones melting I praise him night and day; my golden gem, the Lord, Isa: I will eat him, bite him, and he sets me right.
2980.nuance: The eating and biting are a devotee's hunger for the Lord, as in 2962's fruit. திருத்துவன் may be the Lord correcting the devotee or the devotee savouring him; the subject is unclear.

2981.reading: The mind spread out and drew in: that is great tapas; the mind spread out and drew in: that is the breath; the mind spread out and drew in: that is the abiding soul; the mind that spread out, and speech, died: that is mukti.
2981.nuance: The same movement is named three ways, as tapas, breath and life, and the fourth line ends it. மாதவம் is read as மா தவம், great tapas. The link of mind and breath echoes earlier yogic chapters, where where the mind goes the breath goes.

links.note: 2718 says repeating சிவாய நம and சிவசிவ fixes the mind and is bliss; here the mantra has become a fruit already eaten, and the speaker reports its sweetness.
Both say death can be beaten by those who have the power of tapas: the Kural speaks of leaping past Yama, Tirumular of striking him with the sword of knowledge in a mind where tapas has come.
272 says only those who melt with love can reach 'my gem' (என்பொன் மணி), whatever austerity others do; here the speaker melts to the bone, weeping, and holds 'my golden gem' as his own.

source_issues: 2978: line 2 reads விளக்கிக் தகளிசெய், where the doubled க் before த looks like a misprint (perhaps விளக்குத் தகளி or விளக்கித் தகளி).
2969: line 3, சுத்தும் சிலகும், is obscure and may be corrupt.
